newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli president appeals to Arafat, Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Israeli president appeals to Arafat, Netanyahu.

text.p: Israeli President Ezer Weizman made an emotional plea on Tuesday to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to find the path to peace at a summit in Washington.

"If we don't go the way of peace we'll get tangled here in a war," Weizman said in comments made during a condolence visit to the family of an Israeli soldier killed in last week's Israeli-Palestinian clashes.

"Each side has its own dreams, desires, demands and therefore if we sit together, without the sound of shots and ambulance sirens being heard, perhaps there will be hope," he said in comments broadcast on Israeli radio.
"I hope that we will be intelligent enough to further the peace process that is at the moment foundering a bit.

"I send from here, purposely from here, blessings and wishes to the prime minister and to the chairman, Abu Amar, Arafat, that they find the way to live together and not to shoot at one another," Weizman said using Yasser Arafat's nomme de guerre.
Israel opened a second entrance to a tourist tunnel in Jerusalem near Moslem holy sites last Tuesday, sparking gun battles and clashes that claimed 57 Palestinian and 15 Israeli lives.
President Bill Clinton is hosting a summit between the leaders on Tuesday and Wednesday to try to save the peace process.
